1→# Fog of War — Design Intent
     2→
     3→> The map IS the interface. Everything else gets out of the way.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Core Principle
     8→
     9→Full-canvas experience. Controls float at the edges — translucent, collapsible, Miro-style. GM and Player don't share a layout, but they share this visual language. The map dominates every pixel.
    10→
    11→---
    12→
    13→## Target Devices
    14→
    15→| Device | Role | Input | Priority |
    16→|--------|------|-------|----------|
    17→| Desktop | GM (primary) | Mouse | High |
    18→| Tablet | GM + Player | Touch + stylus | High |
    19→| Phone | Player (join & watch) | Touch | Medium |
    20→
    21→GM fog painting on a phone is not a goal. Tablet with stylus is.
    22→
    23→---
    24→
    25→## Gesture Map
    26→
    27→| Gesture | Action |
    28→|---------|--------|
    29→| 1 finger / stylus | Interact — GM: paint fog; Player: drag token |
    30→| 2-finger drag | Pan the map |
    31→| Pinch | Zoom in/out |
    32→
    33→No mode toggle for pan vs draw. The gesture itself disambiguates. ~100ms grace period before committing to draw, so a second finger can arrive for pan/zoom.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Phases
    38→
    39→### Prep Phase
    40→
    41→The GM has not started the session yet. All panels are expanded. Map management (upload, reorder, delete) happens here. Players see nothing — or a waiting screen — until the GM activates a map.
    42→
    43→### Play Phase
    44→
    45→Controls collapse to minimal state. The map strip shows prev/next arrows for quick switching during play. Full map management is not needed live.
    46→
    47→---
    48→
    49→## Layout: GM
    50→
    51→```
    52→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    53→│ [Adventure Name]    [●●●● +2]          [·]   │  ← topbar: name + avatar stack + status
    54→│                                              │
    55→│ ┃                                            │
    56→│ ┃            F U L L   C A N V A S           │
    57→│ ┃                                            │  ← brush size: vertical slider, left edge
    58→│ ┃                                     [IMG]  │  ← map panel icon, right edge
    59→│                                              │
    60→│ [↩ ↪ Reveal | Fog]                          │  ← undo/redo + mode toggle, bottom-left
    61→└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    62→```
    63→
    64→### Map Panel
    65→
    66→- **Collapsed:** a small icon (image stack) on the right edge. Always accessible.
    67→- **Expanded:** a right-side sheet slides out over the canvas. Contains:
    68→  - Scrollable thumbnail list of all maps
    69→  - Active map highlighted
    70→  - Upload button
    71→  - During play: prev/next arrows at top for quick switching
    72→- Tap icon to open, tap icon or outside to close.
    73→- The sheet overlays the canvas — does not push or resize it.
    74→
    75→> Future idea: if the icon itself could show a tiny stack of map thumbnails (like layered cards), that would be a distinct visual feature worth exploring later.
    76→
    77→### Player Presence (GM topbar)
    78→
    79→Miro-style avatar stack in the GM topbar, right-aligned:
    80→- Overlapping colored circles (player's chosen color + first initial letter).
    81→- Green ring = online. No ring = offline (token persists, player disconnected).
    82→- Overflow counter (`+N`) when more than ~4 players.
    83→- Click a circle → popover with: player name, "Copy player link", "Remove player".
    84→- "Remove player" deletes the token and the player's session. Player would need a new invite to rejoin.
    85→
    86→Tokens are persistent — they belong to the adventure, not the WebSocket session. Disconnecting does not delete the token. Only the GM can remove a player.
    87→
    88→### Controls
    89→
    90→- **Mode toggle** — bottom-left floating pill. Two segments: Reveal / Fog. Always visible. 44pt minimum tap target.
    91→- **Brush size** — vertical slider hugging the left edge, Procreate-style. Drag up = bigger, down = smaller. Shows radius preview on canvas while adjusting.
    92→- **Brush preview** — color-coded circle under cursor/finger. Green tint = reveal, red tint = fog. Strongest mode indicator.
    93→- **Topbar** — adventure name + player presence strip + connection status dot. Always visible but minimal.
    94→
    95→### Collapse Behavior
    96→
    97→Controls are collapsible, never auto-hiding. Each control group has an explicit collapse/expand interaction (tap icon, tap chevron). The user is always in control of what's visible. No timers, no fade-outs.
    98→
    99→- **Always visible:** mode toggle, brush preview (these are too small to need collapsing)
   100→- **Collapsible:** map panel, brush size slider, topbar details
   101→
   102→---
   103→
   104→## Layout: Player
   105→
   106→```
   107→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   108→│ [● PlayerName]                               │  ← corner indicator
   109→│                                              │
   110→│            F U L L   C A N V A S             │
   111→│                                              │
   112→│            (drag your token)                 │
   113→│                                              │
   114→└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   115→```
   116→
   117→- Near-zero UI. Player name + color dot in corner.
   118→- Token drag is the only interaction besides pan/zoom.
   119→- No login, no registration. Player joins via share link, picks name + color. Same player can rejoin from any device — the link is the identity.
   120→
   121→---
   122→
   123→## Session & Token Identity
   124→
   125→No player accounts. The share link is the session key. A player can open the same session on multiple devices simultaneously.
   126→
   127→**Tokens are persistent.** Created when a player first joins, stored in the DB, and survive disconnects. When the same player link reconnects, the existing token is reused — no duplicate. The GM can remove a player (and their token) explicitly.
   128→
   129→**Reconnection flow:**
   130→1. Player opens link → WS connects with `playerLink`.
   131→2. Server checks: does a token exist for this `(adventure_id, player_link)`?
   132→3. Yes → reuse token, mark as online. No → create token.
   133→4. Player disconnects → token stays, marked as offline.
   134→5. GM clicks "Remove player" → token deleted, player would need new invite.
   135→
   136→---
   137→
   138→## Visual Language
   139→
   140→| Property | Value | Why |
   141→|----------|-------|-----|
   142→| Background | `#0d0d1a` dark navy | Recedes, map pops |
   143→| Controls | Translucent, `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)`, 60% opacity bg | Visible but not competing with map |
   144→| Accent | `#4a4aff` blue-purple | Already established |
   145→| Mode: Reveal | Green-tinted brush preview | Intuitive: green = go, clear |
   146→| Mode: Fog | Red-tinted brush preview | Intuitive: red = stop, cover |
   147→| Tap targets | 44pt minimum (Apple HIG) | Fat-finger safe |
   148→| Transitions | 200ms ease-out for expand/collapse | Smooth but not sluggish |
   149→| Control style | Rounded, floating, Miro-inspired | Lightweight, modern, unobtrusive |
   150→
   151→---
   152→
   153→## What This Is NOT
   154→
   155→- Not a phone-first app. Phone players get a functional but not optimized view.
   156→- Not adding features beyond what's in the PoC scope.
   157→- Controls don't float over the canvas center. Edges and corners only.
   158→- No auto-hide. Collapse is explicit, user-initiated.
   159→
   160→---
   161→
   162→## Resolved Decisions
   163→
   164→- **Undo/redo** — two icon buttons next to the mode toggle (bottom-left cluster). Always visible when fog tool is active.
   165→- **Player ping** — long-press gesture on canvas. No dedicated button.
   166→- **Invite link** — accessible via player avatar popover ("Copy player link") in GM topbar.
   167→
   168→## Open Questions
   169→
   170→- **Map stack icon** — could the collapsed map panel icon show a tiny visual stack of the actual map thumbnails? Worth exploring as a polish item.
   171→
